races.paceDynamic: Made U Blush and Love Sonnet will contest the early lead, with Made U Blush's front-running style likely to dominate given Harry Skelton's aggressive approach. The prominent brigade of La Luna Artista, Only One Blue, The Procrastinator, and Queen Maeve will create congestion behind the leaders, setting up tactical complications approaching the business end. This honest gallop from the front two will stretch the field, but the real danger comes from the prominent runners getting first run on the leaders before any hold-up horses can get involved. This race shape strongly favours the prominent runners who can track the pace and strike early, as they'll have positioning advantage over those further back when the race develops.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack gets first run on the fading leaders turning for home
scenarios.body: La Luna Artista, Only One Blue and Cloaks Of Gold will have perfect positioning to exploit any weakening from Made U Blush and Love Sonnet. The class edge of La Luna Artista combined with Only One Blue's proven course form makes them ideally placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Made U Blush and Love Sonnet maintain their duel to the line
scenarios.body: Harry Skelton's tactical nous on Made U Blush will prove decisive as she handles the sustained pace better than Love Sonnet. The Listed winner's class advantage over this handicap field comes to the fore.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Improver Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves too strong and creates opportunities for those held up
scenarios.body: Siorai's tendency to take a strong hold actually helps her close strongly as others tire from the honest gallop. Queen Maeve's big handicapping debut for Dan Skelton could catch the field napping.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders tire dramatically and the race falls apart
scenarios.body: The entire prominent pack will be compromised by following the collapsing pace, leaving The Procrastinator to benefit from any tactical chaos. Whitletts could sneak into contention despite her maiden status.

watchPoints.text: Made U Blush and Love Sonnet must be monitored early - if either gets an uncontested lead the race dynamic changes completely
The prominent pack of La Luna Artista, Only One Blue, The Procrastinator and Queen Maeve creating traffic problems turning for home
Siorai's early position given her tendency to pull hard - if settled further back than usual she becomes more dangerous
Only One Blue and Cloaks Of Gold both representing Max Comley yard with 0/6 recent record - stable confidence key
Harry Skelton choosing Made U Blush over stablemate Queen Maeve signals clear stable preference

races.paceDynamic: Kocktail Bleu, Cosmic Connection, and Desertmore News will all want to go forward early, creating a strong gallop from the start in this 19-runner handicap. The pace should be genuinely testing throughout, particularly with Last Round also likely to track close. This sustained tempo will set up the race perfectly for the hold-up horses who can stay the trip. The strong early gallop favours horses with proven stamina who can quicken late from off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners maintain a strong gallop and tire in the final half-mile
scenarios.body: The strong pace will string out the field and allow patient riders to pick off tiring leaders. Horses like Kapitein Kool, Wilstar, and Dutch Corner are perfectly positioned to benefit from this likely scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent tracker prevails
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent runners can get the perfect trip just behind the leaders
scenarios.body: A horse like Minella Yoga or Kadastral could track the pace without doing too much early work. They can then strike at the optimal moment when the leaders weaken but before the hold-up horses arrive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace collapses early
scenarios.trigger: If the multiple front-runners go too fast and come back to the field quickly
scenarios.body: The strong pace becomes unsustainable and allows a midfield horse to capitalize. This scenario particularly suits horses who can adapt their position and have tactical speed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Wire-to-wire winner
scenarios.trigger: If one of the leaders can dictate on their own terms without serious pressure
scenarios.body: A smart front-runner like Cosmic Connection could potentially steal a march by setting more reasonable fractions. However, with multiple pace pressers, this seems the least likely outcome given the competitive nature.

Kapitein Kool disappointed on handicap debut but the return to a truly-run race could see him bounce back to novice form

races.paceDynamic: Matterhorn and Mahons Glory will contest the early lead, with Matterhorn likely to go forward more aggressively given his recent front-running win at Uttoxeter and Cobden's positive tactics. Mahons Glory made all at Huntingdon but may settle just behind if pressured. The pace should be honest but not excessive with just two confirmed leaders, allowing the race to develop into a proper staying test over the final mile. This setup clearly favours the hold-up horses who can pick up the pieces late, particularly those with proven finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the two leaders set a steady pace and kick clear turning in
scenarios.body: The patient hold-up specialists get the perfect setup to unleash late runs, with Matterhorn and Mahons Glory softening each other up. Blow Your Wad, Etalon, and Doyen Quest all have the class and finishing ability to capitalise.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Matterhorn gets an uncontested lead and controls the tempo
scenarios.body: The Paul Nicholls runner can dictate terms like at Uttoxeter, with Cobden timing the kick perfectly to hold off late challengers. His 5-11 chase record shows he knows how to win when getting his own way.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Ventura Highway shows improved form and tracks the leaders closely
scenarios.body: The former French-trained runner could benefit from being closest to the pace if the hold-up horses leave it too late. His Auteuil win shows he has ability, and the long absence might have freshened him up.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders go too fast early and tie up dramatically
scenarios.body: The race becomes a war of attrition where any finisher can pick up the pieces, potentially suiting the less-fancied runners who get into contention. Form gets thrown out the window in a muddling finish.

watchPoints.text: Matterhorn getting an uncontested lead could be race over if Cobden times the kick right

races.paceDynamic: Thistle Ask will set the tempo from the front, with Solness likely to press or track closely given his own front-running tendencies. The prominently-raced Jonbon, JPR One, Solness, and Mirabad will form the main body, while Edwardstone and Brookie are expected to be held up. With only one confirmed leader in Thistle Ask and no other strong pace angles, this sets up as a moderate gallop that will quicken from the second-last fence. This pace scenario strongly favours the prominent racers and hold-up horses who can unleash finishing kicks, while potentially stretching the stamina of the lone leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustained Gallop Favours Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Thistle Ask maintains a strong gallop throughout and Solness tracks him closely
scenarios.body: The honest pace will set up perfectly for Jonbon and Edwardstone to produce their characteristic finishing bursts from off the speed. Both have the class and tactical speed to benefit when the race becomes a sprint from the last fence.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Thistle Ask and Solness break clear turning for home and maintain their advantage
scenarios.body: The front two will have stolen a march on the field, with Thistle Ask's recent excellent form and Solness's Grade 1 winning ability proving decisive. The closers will struggle to make up the ground in the short Sandown straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Speed Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes stop-start with Solness and Thistle Ask going too slowly early
scenarios.body: The race will become a tactical affair that erupts into a sprint, suiting horses with sharp acceleration. Mirabad's recent Grade 1 success and JPR One's proven ability at this trip will be key assets in a dash to the line.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Benefits Veteran
scenarios.trigger: If Thistle Ask goes too fast early and the pace collapses after the second-last
scenarios.body: Edwardstone's experience and hold-up style will prove crucial as fresher horses tire in front of him. His ability to stay on strongly when others weaken could see him pick up the pieces at a big price.

Jonbon's jumping under pressure given his prominent style and need to be competitive from an early stage
Solness's tactical approach in the early stages will determine if he tracks Thistle Ask or attempts to lead
Edwardstone's positioning turning for home as he needs to be close enough to unleash his finishing effort
Mirabad's early confidence levels given his dramatic odds defying success last time needs backing up

runners_data.spotlight: 2-14 record over fences includes some big runs, including when he hacked up at Ascot (3m5f, good) in November and took second in the Midlands National at Uttoxeter (4m2f, soft) on latest outing; the Ascot race was going this way round but so was his penultimate start when he kept jumping to his left at Musselburgh (12l second to Transmission); that's a niggling concern but he's handicapped to go well if this is another good day.

runners_data.name: Our Power
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 100-day layoff after Scottish National withdrawal, significant fitness concerns despite good ground form
runners_data.comment: Not firing on all cylinders this term; first-time blinkers replace his usual cheekpieces
runners_data.spotlight: Withdrawn from Scottish National last week due to the heavy ground; 6lb lower than this time last year (when third in the Scottish National) as he's not fired on all cylinders this term, but excuses can be made; he's won two major 3m handicaps going right-handed (Ascot and Kempton) on good ground, back in the 2022-23 season admittedly but this 11yo may be dangerous to dismiss, including as first-time blinkers replace his usual cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Road To Home
runners_data.note: Mullins-trained prominent racer also withdrawn from Scottish National, 7yo with upward trajectory but amateur jockey a slight concern
runners_data.comment: Neck 2nd to Ask Brewster in the Kim Muir at Cheltenham (3m2f, good; furthest he's been)
runners_data.spotlight: He was set to be the only Willie Mullins runner in last week's Scottish National but was withdrawn due to the heavy ground; 7yo who was delivered with what seemed a winning challenge under Patrick Mullins in the Kim Muir at Cheltenham (3m2f, good; furthest he's been) six weeks ago only to find that Ask Brewster battled back; up 6lb but has to be in serious calculations.

runners_data.name: Henry's Friend
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who can also lead, wore cheekpieces when winning at Ascot, consistent performer who needs things to fall right
runners_data.comment: Six races in last 14 months were a mixed bag, Ascot 3m win in November the clear highlight
runners_data.spotlight: Seems best making the running or racing prominently; his six races in the last 14 months have been a mixed bag, with an Ascot win (3m, good) in November the highlight; just 1lb higher today and ran respectably on penultimate start, but his two earlier attempts at 3m6f/4m did not work out; a tongue-tie (worn twice in 2023, with a win on first occasion) returns.

runners_data.name: Transmission
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in excellent form after 12-length Edinburgh National win, quick turnaround from 19 days ago could be ideal
runners_data.comment: 12l win at Musselburgh (3m7f) with a first-time visor; fair third to Havaila at Plumpton
runners_data.spotlight: Tapped back into last season's initial promising form, and then some, to win by 12l in the Edinburgh National at Musselburgh (3m7f, good to soft; from Rock My Way) in February with a first-time visor, which has been kept since; ridden by 7lb claimer when fair third off this 8lb higher mark behind Havaila in the Sussex National at Plumpton 19 days ago but needs to hit new heights again.

runners_data.name: Montregard
runners_data.note: Progressive hold-up horse with excellent recent form, half-brother to Protektorat suggests class but 70-day break a slight worry
runners_data.comment: Firmly on upgrade; can prove well handicapped if he gets this trip, which is feasible
runners_data.spotlight: Half-brother to top-class Protektorat; withdrawn from Scottish National last week due to the heavy going; made three notable steps forward on varied ground over 3m at Ascot (unraced here) this season, including for a good prize on latest start when he led two out for a clearcut win; raised another 4lb but he's firmly on the upgrade, likely to prove well handicapped if he gets this trip, which is also feasible; a bold show is on its way.

runners_data.name: Invincible Nao
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist carrying bottom weight, won Sussex National but subsequent form over longer trips has been inconsistent
runners_data.comment: Won over extended 3m4f last term; this from 2lb out of handicap demands big personal best
runners_data.spotlight: Won Sussex National at Plumpton (extended 3m4f, soft) last February in his first long-distance race but less convincing since in forays over 4m2f, C&D and 3m5f; had a small-field 2m4f win on good ground here in November but this race, from 2lb out of the handicap, demands a big personal best.

runners_data.name: In d'Or
runners_data.note: Prominent racer switching yards to Fergal O'Brien, long absence of 98 days raises fitness questions despite previous good form
runners_data.comment: Good third this winter in 3m handicaps here and at Ascot; needs to build on that
runners_data.spotlight: 3m6f for the NH Chase at Cheltenham last March was his only attempt beyond 3m and he was below form; that was also his last run for Venetia Williams (bought for £220,000 in October at the David Maxwell dispersal) and he's been a good third this winter in 3m handicaps here and at Ascot; needs to build on that, as he's edging up the weights, but he's not fully exposed.

runners_data.name: Havaila
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with serious momentum from recent wins, 19-day turnaround looks ideal for maintaining his current purple patch
runners_data.comment: Won easily by 7l at Newbury and 5l at Plumpton (3m5f Sussex National, good) last two races
runners_data.spotlight: A rising force in the last 15 months and that's gained serious momentum in his last two starts, when winning easily by 7l at Newbury (extended 2m7f, good to soft) and 5l in the Sussex National at Plumpton (3m5f, good); strong-travelling sort who's now seeing out his races really well too; up another 10lb but could still have more in the locker.

runners_data.name: Gabbys Cross
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse wearing cheekpieces, hasn't won since 2022 but showed promise at Newbury and quick turnaround suits
runners_data.comment: Jumped poorly on heavy in Scottish National (40-1) last week; this race also looks tough
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-Irish 11yo (six races for current yard) who has not won since 2022 but went close with first-time cheekpieces (kept since) over 3m2f at Newbury in February; second of three at Ascot (3m) in another veterans' race next time was creditable in the end, after he'd been detached at one point; that helps to envisage him as a stayer but he jumped poorly on heavy in Scottish National (40-1, pulled up) last week and this race also looks tough.

runners_data.name: Livin On Luco
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who will control the tempo, made all at Fontwell but needs to maintain gallop for longer here
runners_data.comment: Commendable over 3m3f/3m7f in three of his four starts this season; place claims
runners_data.spotlight: Failed to fire in the Eider at Newcastle on penultimate start; commendable otherwise this season, making all in the Southern National at Fontwell (3m3f, good to soft), fourth in Welsh Grand National at Chepstow (3m7f, good to soft) and short-headed at Exeter (3m7f, good) five weeks ago; raised another 2lb but has place claims.

runners_data.name: Ask Brewster
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with excellent Cheltenham form, amateur rider claims valuable 7lb and record over trip is very strong
runners_data.comment: Bit to prove right-handed but otherwise lots to like, likely to be suited by trip/ground
runners_data.spotlight: 3m4f resulted in an 8l win at Cheltenham last April and he's won over 3m/3m2f in two of his three starts this season; latest was the Kim Muir at Cheltenham in which he was always front rank under Shane Cotter and responded admirably when Road To Home joined him on the run-in; up 7lb but this trip makes plenty of appeal and all five chase wins have been on good ground or good to firm (withdrawn from Scottish National last week due to the heavy); has a bit to prove going right-handed, with a run here in December prompting concern, but otherwise lots to like.

races.paceDynamic: Livin On Luco will control this from the front with no other confirmed pace-setters willing to challenge his lead, creating a sustainable gallop that builds gradually. The prominent racers Rock My Way, Road To Home, Our Power and In d'Or will likely track within 3-4 lengths but won't apply early pressure. Over this stamina-sapping 3m4½f trip on good ground, the lack of pace pressure means the race will develop into a staying test where those who can quicken off the steady tempo will thrive. This tactical setup clearly favours hold-up horses who can unleash a sustained finish, as the moderate early pace will leave plenty in reserve for the closing stages.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace remains steady with Livin On Luco unopposed in front.
scenarios.body: The patient tactics allow hold-up specialists to conserve energy before unleashing their finishing kicks, with the good ground helping their acceleration. Multiple closers will have every chance to time their runs perfectly off the moderate gallop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front End Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Livin On Luco sets too strong a pace or the prominent trackers apply unexpected pressure.
scenarios.body: The early tempo becomes unsustainable, causing the leaders and prominent racers to weaken dramatically in the final mile. This opens the door for the most patient hold-up horses who have conserved maximum energy.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Rock My Way or Road To Home can track the leader perfectly and kick approaching the final fence.
scenarios.body: These prominent racers get the ideal trip behind the steady pace and have enough left to outstay the hold-up horses. Their tactical positioning proves superior to both the tired leader and the horses coming from too far back.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Sustainable Pace Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Livin On Luco maintains his rhythm and the field fails to mount a serious challenge.
scenarios.body: The front-runner's controlled tempo never cracks and he proves too strong when the closers finally make their moves. His fitness and tactical advantage from making his own running throughout becomes decisive.

watchPoints.text: Livin On Luco could set too strong a pace early and compromise his stamina reserves for the final mile climb
Our Power and Road To Home both carry fitness concerns after 100-day and Scottish National withdrawal respectively
Rock My Way could get caught in traffic if the pace collapses and multiple hold-up horses come with late runs
Havaila's recent purple patch and quick 19-day turnaround could make him the most progressive horse in the field
Ask Brewster's 7lb amateur allowance gives him a significant weight advantage in this competitive handicap

races.name: bet365 Select Hurdle (Grade 2) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Jingko Blue
runners_data.note: Prominent runner from the Henderson stable with good recent 2m4f-2m5f form, suits the trip and going
runners_data.comment: One of the main contenders, albeit may struggle to reverse placings with Kabral Du Mathan
runners_data.spotlight: Has shown good form over 2m4f/2m5f at Cheltenham this term, finishing second to Kabral Du Mathan in Grade 2 and recording an emphatic success from the front in Festival handicap; failed to get home in 3m Grade 1 at Aintree last time; one of the main contenders, back down in distance.

runners_data.name: Kabral Du Mathan
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse perfectly suited to the likely tactical pace, 44 days since last run could be ideal for peak fitness
runners_data.comment: Has become an exciting force for current stable and is the one to beat, back down in trip
runners_data.spotlight: An exciting force since joining current stable and sent beyond 2m, gaining impressive wins at Haydock (2m3f handicap) and Cheltenham (2m4f Grade 2) then shaping like the best horse in the Grade 1 Stayers' Hurdle (3m) until his tank emptied late on; the one to beat, back down in trip.

runners_data.name: Lucky Place
runners_data.note: Prominent style but dual Grade 2 winner looks below his best recent form, 45-day break a concern
runners_data.comment: Finished behind Kabral Du Mathan and Jingko Blue on penultimate start
runners_data.spotlight: Dual Grade 2 winner last term; finished third at the same level on penultimate start but was behind Kabral Du Mathan and stablemate Jingko Blue in that Cheltenham race; seems set for another bronze medal at best.

runners_data.name: Rubaud
runners_data.note: Front-runner who will dictate the pace uncontested, but trip extension beyond his usual 2m pattern is questionable
runners_data.comment: Raced mostly at about 2m and isn't crying out for this step back up in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Form dipped in Cheltenham Festival handicap returned to fences last time; multiple Grade 2 winner but has raced mostly at about 2m and isn't crying out for this step back up in trip; first go beyond a sharp 2m4f.

runners_data.name: French Ship
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with form concerns after three poor efforts, needs to recapture his autumn progressive profile
runners_data.comment: Form has gone awry in last three starts but progressive otherwise; may rebound
runners_data.spotlight: Form has gone rather awry in last three outings but he has been progressive otherwise, culminating in 2m4f handicap wins at Cheltenham and Newbury in the autumn; may rebound and run a good race.

runners_data.name: Altobelli
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 99-day break, tactical style suits the likely race shape but fitness query
runners_data.comment: Latest effort suggests this scenario will prove ideal; could go well
runners_data.spotlight: Completed a 2m3f handicap double at Ascot last season; best effort since when second in useful event at Windsor (2m4f) on last appearance, leaving the impression today's scenario will prove ideal; could go well.

races.paceDynamic: Rubaud will take the field along from the front with no pressure, setting a comfortable rhythm over this extended 2m5½f trip. The prominently-raced trio of Jingko Blue, Lucky Place and French Ship will sit in behind the leader, while hold-up horses Kabral Du Mathan and Altobelli will be positioned towards the rear. With only one confirmed front-runner and a moderate gallop likely, this race shape strongly favours the hold-up horses who can unleash late finishing kicks, particularly Kabral Du Mathan who has thrived when allowed to come from behind.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Rubaud sets an undemanding pace and the race becomes tactical
scenarios.body: The prominent runners will be left flat-footed when the hold-up horses unleash their finishing kicks in the final half-mile. Kabral Du Mathan and Altobelli will have too much late pace for the early positioned horses.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent runner stays on
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is steady but one prominent horse finds extra
scenarios.body: Jingko Blue or Lucky Place could time their effort perfectly from their tracking positions behind Rubaud. Their class tells in a sustained drive from two furlongs out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Rubaud leads throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Rubaud's stamina and tactical advantage proves decisive at this longer trip
scenarios.body: The Paul Nicholls-trained leader capitalizes on the lack of early pace pressure to dictate terms throughout. His front-running style could be hard to peg back if he finds extra at this extended distance.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: French Ship bounces back
scenarios.trigger: If French Ship rediscovers his autumn form when relaxing off the pace
scenarios.body: The Philip Hobbs runner sheds his recent poor efforts and produces the form that won at Cheltenham and Newbury. His prominent style allows him to strike at the right moment.

watchPoints.text: Kabral Du Mathan could have too much finishing speed if Rubaud sets a pedestrian pace from the front
Jingko Blue's prominent position behind the leader could leave him vulnerable to late closers in a slowly-run race
Lucky Place may struggle to quicken from his prominent position if the pace becomes tactical
French Ship needs to travel kindly in behind to suggest his form revival is genuine
Altobelli's finishing kick after his long break will indicate whether he can compete at this level fresh

races.name: bet365 Josh Gifford Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Calimystic
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with low mileage who won here last month but was recently withdrawn due to good ground concerns, now faces that exact condition.
runners_data.comment: Scored over 3m here last month and is now 2-2 over fences; should have more to offer
runners_data.spotlight: Low-mileage 7yo who is 2-2 over fences, the latter win gained here (3m, soft) last month; recently withdrawn with good ground deemed unsuitable but his first two wins (one over hurdles) were gained on good; should cope with this drop back in trip and has plenty of scope for further progress; respected.

runners_data.name: Millforce
runners_data.note: Prominent type switching to Henry Oliver with limited recent form (1/11 T14) and was pulled up on stable debut at Haydock after Irish success.
runners_data.comment: Won in Ireland in the autumn but pulled up on stable debut just ten days ago
runners_data.spotlight: Signed off for Gavin Cromwell in Ireland with hard-fought win at Galway (2m6f, yielding) in the autumn but was pulled up when reappearing for new stable at Haydock (3m1f, good to soft) ten days ago and needs to turn things around quickly.

runners_data.name: Kahavari
runners_data.note: Prominent racer fitted with tongue-tie seeking first chase win in 13 attempts, but has been consistently placed in three recent chase efforts.
runners_data.comment: Clear second at Kelso this month but is 3lb higher in a stronger race here
runners_data.spotlight: 0-13 since winning over hurdles on debut in France in 2024; runner-up in three chases since fitted with a tongue-tie this year, most recently at Kelso (2m7f, good) three weeks ago, but he is 3lb higher in a stronger race here and needs to find something extra.

runners_data.name: Go West
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner with 63-day absence following poor jumping display at Kempton, but previously effective at this trip with tactical advantage.
runners_data.comment: Didn't jump well enough last time; contender if judged on Musselburgh win two runs ago
runners_data.spotlight: Didn't jump well enough when well beaten in Kempton Grade 2 novice in February last time but had doubled his chasing tally with ready success at Musselburgh (2m4f, good to soft) three weeks earlier, and will be dangerous if back in similar form.

runners_data.name: Palamon
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who returned to form with tongue-tie refitted at Bangor last month, faces tactical disadvantage in likely steady-pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Landed a big punt at Bangor last month and could still be well treated after 10lb hike
runners_data.spotlight: Returned to form and rewarded heavy market support at Bangor (2m4f, good; tongue-tie refitted) last month, his fifth start for Dan Skelton; just a respectable sixth under penalty in the Red Rum at Aintree (2m, good to soft) nine days later and his mark is another 5lb higher here, but he remains very much of interest.

races.paceDynamic: Go West will control proceedings from the front with his confirmed leading tendencies, likely unopposed in a small field where Calimystic, Millforce and Kahavari all prefer prominent positions but won't challenge for the early lead. The Paul Nicholls-trained leader should dictate a steady, sustainable pace without pressure, creating ideal conditions for his front-running style. With only hold-up specialist Palamon racing from behind, this race strongly favours front runners and prominent racers who can track the pace and challenge late without needing to make up significant ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Go West jumps cleanly and maintains his rhythm from the front.
scenarios.body: The 8-year-old can exploit his tactical advantage with no genuine pace pressure, building an insurmountable lead over the final fences. His class edge (OR 139) combined with perfect tactical positioning proves decisive in a race run to suit.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes Late
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent runners can match Go West's pace and outfinish him.
scenarios.body: Calimystic or Millforce can sit in Go West's slipstream before unleashing a telling challenge, with their fresher finishing kick overcoming the leader's tactical advantage. The pace scenario still favours these prominent types over the hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Defies Shape
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely strong or Go West fades dramatically after his long absence.
scenarios.body: Palamon can exploit a collapse up front, with his proven stamina and Dan Skelton's 12/36 recent form helping him pick up the pieces. However, this requires the race to fall apart ahead of him, which seems unlikely given the small field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Outsider Victory
scenarios.trigger: If multiple favourites underperform or jumping errors eliminate the leaders.
scenarios.body: Kahavari finally breaks his chase duck in a race where the main fancies fail to deliver, exploiting his tongue-tie advantage and recent consistent placing record. This scenario requires multiple things to go wrong for the market leaders.

watchPoints.text: Go West's jumping accuracy after his poor display at Kempton where he didn't jump well enough and was well beaten.
Calimystic's handling of good ground having been recently withdrawn when conditions were deemed unsuitable for him.
Millforce's adaptation to new trainer Henry Oliver following his pulled-up effort on stable debut at Haydock.
Palamon's ability to get into contention from his hold-up style if the pace becomes genuinely searching early on.
Kahavari breaking his chase duck after 13 winless attempts despite consistent recent placing efforts with tongue-tie fitted.

races.name: bet365 Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Favour And Fortune
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with career-best recent form but faces major tactical disadvantage in this crowded field
runners_data.comment: Career-best form when close third of 22 at Aintree a fortnight ago
runners_data.spotlight: Seen only twice this season but posted career-best performance when close third of 22 at Aintree (2m4f, good to soft) a fortnight ago, despite Tom Bellamy's saddle slipping after the last; respected.

runners_data.name: Authorised Speed
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 714-day absence, course winner but fitness must be questioned
runners_data.comment: Placed off 7lb higher in this race two years ago; returns from long layoff today
runners_data.spotlight: Dual 2m winner here; absent since finishing fifth in a beginners' chase in May 2024 but was placed off mark 7lb higher than today's in this race two years ago (good ground); worth a glance in the market.

runners_data.name: Dargiannini
runners_data.note: Prominent style but pulled up twice since winning, headgear changes suggest problems
runners_data.comment: Narrow winner off today's mark in October but pulled up both starts since
runners_data.spotlight: Returned from a break with narrow win at Uttoxter (2m4f, good) in October but pulled up on both starts since, latterly at last month's Cheltenham Festival; younger rivals have much more persuasive profiles.

runners_data.name: Royal Way
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in excellent current form, perfectly suited by race shape and conditions
runners_data.comment: Won off reduced mark last month and ran well in defeat ten days later
runners_data.spotlight: Exploited reduced mark when winning quite comfortably at Ludlow last month and was one of two to pull clear of the others when second at Ascot (also 2m5f, good) ten days later; no surprise if he features.

runners_data.name: Fasol
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with amateur jockey, strong recent form but 5lb claim valuable here

runners_data.name: Surrey Lord
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 98-day break, needs luck in running from back
runners_data.comment: Made good progress towards end of 2025 (three wins); returns from a short break
runners_data.spotlight: Made good progress towards end of 2025, with latest of three wins gained at Kempton (2m5f, good) on Boxing Day; not discredited when fourth at Ascot (2m3f, soft) in January and has good claims if tuned up after a break.

runners_data.name: Trustintimes
runners_data.note: Prominent racer stepping up in trip after Aintree disappointment, versatile style helps
runners_data.comment: 3-5 hurdles; below form when upped to 2m4f this month but may still have potential
runners_data.spotlight: 3-5 over hurdles, the latest win gained at Ascot (1m7f, good) in November; never really got involved when upped to 2m4f at Aintree a fortnight ago but could plausibly still have untapped potential over this trip.

runners_data.name: Listentoyourheart
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with class but needs race to develop favorably, Skelton booking positive
runners_data.comment: Landed big prize at Windsor on New Year's Day but not quite in same form either run since
runners_data.spotlight: Just held on to land big prize at Windsor (2m4f, good) on New Year's Day but wasn't in quite the same form on next two outings (2m3f/3m) and probably needs to find hidden reserves.

runners_data.name: Joltin N Jiving
runners_data.note: Non-runner, would have been lone pace-setter

runners_data.name: Gnomon
runners_data.note: Prominent Flat recruit with upward hurdles trajectory, race shape suits perfectly
runners_data.comment: Cosily won small-field Ascot maiden in March; could easily have more to offer in handicaps
runners_data.spotlight: Fairly useful Flat racer; runner-up on first three hurdle starts (all 2m) before cruising clear in four-runner Ascot maiden (2m3f, good) last month; could easily have more improvement to come in handicap hurdles; interesting.

runners_data.name: No Ordinary Joe
runners_data.note: Prominent racer trying headgear again, trip increase should help but form patchy
runners_data.comment: Ran well at Aintree a fortnight ago but his last win came in 2022; others preferred
runners_data.spotlight: Kept on for sixth of 21 in first-time visor at Aintree (2m, good to soft) a fortnight ago and will be suited by this move back up in trip, but his last win came in 2022 and he's patently not the force of old.

runners_data.name: Lucky Manifest
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose progress stalled, needs to recapture autumn form
runners_data.comment: Did well in the autumn but progress has stalled since; given wind op last month
runners_data.spotlight: Started off for new stable in excellent form in the autumn, winning at Kelso (2m6f, good) before big-field second at Cheltenham (2m5f, soft), but his progress has stalled a bit since; needs combination of last month's wind op and first-time tongue-tie to have positive effect.

runners_data.name: Tour Ovalie
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse trying longer trip, workable mark but tactical disadvantage
runners_data.comment: Ran quite well at Chepstow last month and Sean Bowen takes over today; a possible
runners_data.spotlight: Gained all six hurdle wins at around 2m but ran quite well when fourth at Chepstow (2m3f, soft) last month; current mark is workable (even from 1lb out of the weights) and Sean Bowen takes over today; could have a say.

runners_data.name: Aurigny Mill
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in good form, needs significant pace collapse to be effective
runners_data.comment: Good winner at Taunton two starts ago but others in this field look better handicapped
runners_data.spotlight: Seemingly back in prime form when clear winner at Taunton (2m, heavy) in February; also suited by good ground and stays at least 2m3f but he disappointed on latest outing and others in this field look better handicapped.

runners_data.name: Last Kingdom
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse completely out of form for new trainer, hard to recommend
runners_data.comment: Out of form for new stable this year but the refitted cheekpieces might aid his cause
runners_data.spotlight: Won big-field Listed handicap in first-time cheekpieces at Listowel (2m, good to yielding) for Willie Mullins in September; badly out of form for new stable this year (four runs) but may fare better now that the cheekpieces are reinstated.

runners_data.name: Across Earth
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with consistent recent form, only 10 days since last run
runners_data.comment: 2m winner here in December; still in good form; considered on first attempt at 2m4f
runners_data.spotlight: Won against his own age-group here (2m, soft; also suited by good) in December and has finished close up on all three outings since (1m7f-2m); must be considered on this first attempt at 2m4f.

races.paceDynamic: With Joltin N Jiving withdrawn, the early pace will be set by the prominent racers Authorised Speed, Dargiannini, Royal Way, Fasol, Trustintimes, Gnomon, No Ordinary Joe, Lucky Manifest, and Across Earth - creating a crowded and competitive early gallop. This congested front group will likely produce a solid but not breakneck tempo over the first circuit, with multiple horses vying for position. The hold-up brigade including Favour And Fortune, Surrey Lord, Listentoyourheart, Tour Ovalie, Aurigny Mill, and Last Kingdom will have plenty of cover but may struggle to find clear racing room in the straight with 16 runners. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can secure good positions early and avoid traffic problems, while the pure hold-up horses face a significant tactical disadvantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Racers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the large group of prominent racers maintain strong positions without excessive early pace.
scenarios.body: The leaders will string out naturally over 2m4f, allowing the best prominent racers to dictate from ideal positions while hold-up horses get trapped behind the wall of runners. Royal Way, Gnomon, and Across Earth are perfectly positioned to exploit this scenario from their forward berths.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Hero Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or the prominent group goes too fast early and comes back dramatically.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where patient tactics pay off, allowing the best hold-up horses with tactical speed to weave through and strike late. Favour And Fortune and Listentoyourheart have the class to capitalize when getting the right scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Battle Unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent racers engage in a pace duel that sets up the race for closers.
scenarios.body: The early battle between Authorised Speed, Fasol, and others will create the perfect setup for horses held up with one run, particularly those with proven finishing kicks. Lucky Manifest and Aurigny Mill can benefit from this aggressive early tempo despite wide draws.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Traffic Issues
scenarios.trigger: If the large field creates significant interference and racing room becomes scarce in the straight.
scenarios.body: Multiple fallers or severe traffic problems will benefit only the horses who secure clear runs, likely those who commit to forward positions early or get extreme luck in running. Trustintimes and No Ordinary Joe have the experience to navigate trouble.

watchPoints.text: Royal Way and Gnomon could dominate if securing ideal prominent positions early without pressure
Favour And Fortune may struggle to find racing room despite class advantage in this large field
Trustintimes stepping up significantly in trip after failing over 2m4f at Aintree last time

Authorised Speed returning after nearly two years off but has strong course record to draw upon
